subject: Set difference in Stan (or dropping by index)

messages.author: f4eb3507bb54a5e7
messages.subject: Set difference in Stan (or dropping by index)
parts:
I'm repeating a question I posed here on Stack Overflow.

I can't seem to figure out the best way to drop a column by index in Stan.

I have a matrix and I want to get all but one column of the matrix. For example, in R I would do the following:

    # Some matrix X
    X = matrix(nrow = 10, ncol = 4)

    # Approach 1 with setdiff
    X[, setdiff(1:ncol(X), 3)]

    # Direct approach in R
    X[, -3]

I cannot figure out the right way to do the same thing in Stan. Simple question, but any advice would help.

Thank you in advance, and sorry if this basic question has been answered elsewhere but I couldn't find it via google or the documentation.
Luke Sonnet

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Set difference in Stan (or dropping by index)
parts:
There's no setdiff, and while you could build up
that set, you can also just do this:

append_col(a[ , 1:2], a[ , 4:4])

to append two submatrices together by column.
In general, that's

append_col(a[ , 1:(n-1)], a[ , (n+1):N])

but you have to watch out for n = 1 or n = N side
conditions.

- Bob
